newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish banker calls for more investment incentives.
newsitem.headline: Irish banker calls for more investment incentives.

text.p: Incentives should be put in place to attract private and institutional investors to invest in small Irish companies, the managing director of Ireland's ICC Bank said on Friday.
Michael Quinn told IBEC's industrial policy committee that there were a large and increasing number of Irish companies with excellent potential which needed equity to fund growth.
But he said there was a worrying "equity gap" in the Irish capital market which must be addressed as a matter of urgency.

"Because of the small size of the Irish Stock Exchange and because trading is generally concentrated in the ten largest companies, it is now difficult to raise equity on the capital markets in Ireland," he said.

He noted that the Irish Stock Exchange had recognised the problem and was seeking to establish a Developing Companies Market to replicate the success of the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in London.
"It is hoped that through a combination of incentives and less onerous listing requirements that more companies will be encouraged to raise capital on the capital markets in Ireland," he said.
